title: Germany: Voting underway in two key state elections
summary: Elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania are expected to bring gains for the far-right AfD party and could determine whether Chancellor Friedrich Merz can hold on to power. Follow DW…

image.caption: A voter casts their ballot at a Berlin Bierhaus ('beer house') that will serve as a polling stationImage: Fabrizio Bensch/REUTERS

blocks.text: Candidates cast votes in key state elections

Voters have been lining up at polling stations to cast their ballots, as have the candidates (presumably to vote for themselves) in Berlin and in the northeastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
In the German capital, Werner Graf (Green Party) and Steffen Krach (center-left Social Democrats) cast their votes in the Tempelhof-Schöneberg constituency.

blocks.caption: Werner Graf, the co-leader of the Greens, submits his ballotImage: Annette Riedl/dpa/picture alliance
Steffen Krach (SPD) casts his vote in BerlinImage: Christoph Soeder/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Further north, Leif-Erik Holm (far-right AfD) cast his vote in Schwerin, the capital of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
Holm told local public broadcaster NDR outside the polling station that he was "optimistic" about his party's chances.
"The clouds have parted and the sky is turning blue," he said, referring to the color of his party.

blocks.caption: Leif-Erik Holm (AfD) casts his vote in Schwerin, Mecklenburg-Western PomeraniaImage: Annegret Hilse/REUTERS

blocks.text: His rival, the incumbent state premier Manuela Schwesig of the Social Democrats (SPD), cast her vote a short time later.

blocks.caption: Schwesig said she hopes the election will 'send a strong message and that it will be a good day for our country'Image: Lisi Niesner/REUTERS
